features.title: authSession runs on an async StorageAdapter
features.description: StorageAdapter { get, set, remove } returns promises. The web passes a localStorage adapter, and an extension can pass chrome.storage.local.
steps: Unit test: an in-memory adapter round-trips persist/read/clear
Unit test: an adapter that throws on get/set does not crash the caller, and reads come back as null
npm run build (client) passes — erasableSyntaxOnly
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-19 by authSession.test.ts (16 tests). DESIGN DEVIATION from spec P1 step 2, taken on purpose: the adapter is async, but authSession keeps an in-memory cache, so the getters stay SYNC. initSession() fills the cache before React mounts (main.tsx; .then is a style choice — Vite 7's default target does support top-level await, and an earlier comment claiming otherwise was corrected in P2). adapter.subscribe feeds other contexts' writes into the cache. This avoided pushing await into axios, socket handshakes and first render (R4). Writes update memory synchronously and persistTokens can be awaited; refreshOnce awaits it (R3). The throwing adapter reads as signed out, and the lazy localStorage lookup keeps a blocked store from crashing at startup. npm run build passes.

1b1955b: the dedupe count was uncapped; the server rejects count > 10000 with a 400, which the circuit breaker does not count as a failure

features.title: Worker stopped with events queued: none lost, none doubled
features.description: A persisted queue in chrome.storage.session; a 30s alarm retries.
steps: Server (proxy) down: the batch is in the queue
Worker stopped from chrome:// or edge://serviceworker-internals
Server back, nothing pokes the worker: the event arrives once, from a FRESH worker (in-memory marker gone), and the queue is empty
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-20, Chrome and Edge, 14/14 each. Two harness findings worth keeping. (1) With Puppeteer's DevTools session still attached, a stopped extension worker is NEVER woken again (0 requests in 45s), so the check detaches first. (2) ServiceWorker.stopAllWorkers and Target.closeTarget do not stop an extension worker. Edge renders the stop control as <cr-button data-command="stop">, not <button>: the first Edge run reported the worker "not stopped", and its "arrives once" pass was therefore meaningless; the marker check exists to catch exactly that. LIMITS by design: delivery is at-least-once (a worker stopped between the 202 and the queue write resends), and storage.session means a full BROWSER restart drops queued events.

features.title: Finding the API needs no permission prompt
features.description: The web app serves /apexops.json with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so the worker can read it before any site access exists. If a host does not send it, the popup asks for access to that site and retries.
steps: against the shipped build with zero origins granted: a pasted project URL resolves to the API and the grant list is still empty afterwards
the response is readable cross-origin from the extension
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-21. This removes one of the two prompts in the connect flow; the remaining one covers the API and the site together. ACAO itself cannot be asserted from JS (it is not a readable response header), so what is checked is that the read succeeds.

features.title: Connecting starts capturing the open tab, with no reload
features.description: Registered content scripts only run on a navigation, so the tab a person just connected would stay silent until reloaded. The worker injects both scripts into that tab once; each sets a marker in its own world and returns early if it is already there.
steps: after connect, an error fired WITHOUT reloading becomes an issue
after a reload the registered scripts take over and each error is still counted once (no double capture)
FAILURE CASE: with the injection disabled, only the no-reload case fails (33/34)
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-21 in the p4 check, 34/34. The popup says which of the two happened ("being captured now" vs "reload the site").

features.title: Toolbar icons
features.description: scripts/make-icons.mjs draws the web app mark (lime #C5F43A ground, dark activity pulse) at 16/32/48/96/128 and writes public/icon/*.png. No image dependency: PNG chunks plus zlib, shapes by distance field at 4x.
steps: the manifest carries all five sizes
the 128px file was read back as an image and looks like the sidebar mark
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-21. Lime is the background rather than the glyph so the icon stays visible in a dark toolbar. The PNGs are committed; re-run `npm run icons` to regenerate.

features.title: A password is never sent to a server that has not said it is ApexOps
features.description: GET /api/health now answers app: 'apexops', and the extension checks it before POSTing credentials.
steps: unit: a 404 (another project on that port), a plain {status:ok}, and an app:"other" each refuse with not-apexops-api, send no login request, and store nothing
unit: an unreachable server is a network problem and still sends nothing
in the browser, against the real dev servers: a web app naming a non-ApexOps API is refused and that server received nothing at all
Mutations: skipping the check, or accepting any 200, each turn the refusal tests red
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-22. This exists because :3000 on this machine is sometimes held by another project (see memory): the address comes from a web app's /apexops.json, and without a marker an ApexOps password would be posted to a stranger's login route and reported as a wrong password. It is a mistake-catcher, NOT authentication — any server can serve the string; what it rules out is the wrong-port case.

features.title: Ready to use on this machine: the whole flow against the developer's own dev servers
features.description: checks/ready-dev.mjs runs the popup, worker and API against client :5173 + API :3000 (not the rig), on a cleared extension profile.
steps: the API on :3000 identifies itself and its database is connected; /apexops.json names that same API
the sign-in step names the real host; connect succeeds and reports capturing without a reload
console.error on the site becomes an issue in the project
the extension session is labelled; disconnect and sign out leave nothing behind
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-22: 8/8 in Chrome 131 against the live dev setup, project "test", issue #435 in 5.3s. Uses the e2e build because the permission dialog is native UI; everything else is the shipped path. Rerun with READY_APP/READY_API for other ports.

features.title: Building while the extension is loaded
features.description: Windows refuses to wipe the output folder a browser has open (EBUSY), which is the normal state once someone has loaded it unpacked.
steps: WXT_OUT_DIR=<path> builds elsewhere instead
the guide says to reload the extension card after any build
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-22: reproduced against the folder the user had loaded (the shipped build was a day stale and locked), and the override built cleanly with the new health check inside. Not a code defect — a Windows file-lock fact that costs ten confusing minutes.
